entries.name: claude-code
entries.title: Claude Code
entries.description: Anthropic's agentic coding tool for the terminal

unsupported.riscv64: Anthropic publishes Claude Code for x64 and arm64 only

entries.verify: sha256 pinned by KwickOS; equal to the per-platform checksum in the vendor's manifest.json (stable channel)
entries.upstream_install: curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash (downloads the same binary and checks it against manifest.json)
entries.first_run: run 'claude' in a project folder and sign in, or store a key: kwick-agents key set claude-code ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
entries.notes: The built-in auto-updater is turned off; 'kwick-agents update' moves to the next pinned stable release.

entries.name: codex
entries.title: Codex CLI
entries.description: OpenAI's lightweight coding agent for the terminal

unsupported.riscv64: OpenAI publishes Codex for x86_64 and aarch64 only

entries.verify: sha256 pinned by KwickOS; equal to the GitHub release asset digest
entries.upstream_install: npm install -g @openai/codex, or the install.sh release asset (codex-package tarball checked against codex-package_SHA256SUMS)
entries.first_run: run 'codex' and sign in with ChatGPT, or: kwick-agents key set codex OPENAI_API_KEY
entries.notes: Codex has its own command sandbox; inside the KwickOS sandbox it may report that it cannot nest one. Then start it with 'codex --sandbox danger-full-access', which is still confined by the KwickOS sandbox.

entries.name: gemini-cli
entries.title: Gemini CLI
entries.description: Google's open-source AI agent for the terminal
entries.verify: sha256 pinned by KwickOS; equal to the GitHub release asset digest. Runs on the pinned Node.js runtime
entries.first_run: run 'gemini' and sign in with Google, or: kwick-agents key set gemini-cli GEMINI_API_KEY
entries.notes: Pure JavaScript, so it also runs on riscv64 (Node.js from unofficial-builds.nodejs.org).

entries.name: opencode
entries.title: opencode
entries.description: Open-source coding agent for the terminal with any model provider

unsupported.riscv64: opencode publishes x64 and arm64 builds only

entries.verify: sha256 pinned by KwickOS; equal to the GitHub release asset digest (the vendor publishes no checksum file for v1)
entries.upstream_install: curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash (no checksum check), or npm install -g opencode-ai
entries.first_run: run 'opencode' and connect a provider with /connect, or store a provider key with kwick-agents key set
entries.notes: Pinned to the v1 line, which GitHub, npm and https://opencode.ai/install mark as latest. The v2 line installs from https://opencode.ai/v2/install.

entries.name: omp
entries.title: oh-my-pi (omp)
entries.description: Coding-first agent built from Mario Zechner's pi, with MCP, LSP and many providers

unsupported.riscv64: oh-my-pi publishes x64 and arm64 builds only

entries.verify: sha256 pinned by KwickOS; equal to the vendor's SHA256SUMS.txt in the GitHub release
entries.upstream_install: curl -fsSL https://omp.sh/install | sh (binary from build.stencil.so, sha256 checked), or bun install -g @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent
entries.first_run: run 'omp' and sign in with /login, or store a provider key with kwick-agents key set omp ...

entries.name: openclaw
entries.title: OpenClaw
entries.description: Personal AI assistant with a local gateway, messaging channels and a web Control UI

unsupported.riscv64: several native modules (sqlite-vec, node-pty, fs-safe) have no riscv64 build

entries.verify: npm ci checks the sha512 of every package against the package-lock.json that KwickOS ships (439 tarballs; the rest are bundled inside them); install scripts run in a sandbox without network
entries.upstream_install: curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash (installs Node.js through NodeSource with sudo, build tools, then npm install -g)
entries.first_run: run 'openclaw onboard' to configure a model, then 'openclaw gateway' (Control UI on http://127.0.0.1:18789)
entries.notes: The gateway is not installed as a system service; start it with 'openclaw gateway' inside the sandbox.

entries.name: hermes
entries.title: Hermes Agent
entries.description: Self-improving AI agent with skills, memory, cron jobs and messaging gateways

unsupported.riscv64: Hermes supports x86_64 and aarch64 only

entries.verify: git tag checked against the pinned commit; Python packages installed by 'uv sync --frozen' with the sha256 hashes in the project's uv.lock; Python itself checked by uv
entries.upstream_install: curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash (git clone, uv, its own PM for Node.js and Chromium, a gateway service)
entries.first_run: run 'hermes setup' to pick a model provider, or: kwick-agents key set hermes OPENROUTER_API_KEY
entries.notes: Optional extras that the upstream installer adds (browser tools with Chromium, TTS) are not installed.

entries.name: aider
entries.title: Aider
entries.description: AI pair programming in your terminal, works with git

unsupported.riscv64: several dependencies publish no riscv64 wheels

entries.verify: uv pip install --require-hashes with a hash-locked requirements file that KwickOS ships (109 packages); Python 3.12 checked by uv
entries.upstream_install: uv tool install --python python3.12 aider-chat@latest, or curl -LsSf https://aider.chat/install.sh | sh
entries.first_run: store a key (kwick-agents key set aider ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) and run 'aider' in a git repository

entries.name: goose
entries.title: Goose
entries.description: Open-source, extensible AI agent with MCP extensions

unsupported.riscv64: Goose publishes x86_64 and aarch64 builds only

entries.verify: sha256 pinned by KwickOS; equal to the GitHub release asset digest (the vendor publishes no checksum file)
entries.first_run: run 'goose configure' to choose a provider; keys from 'kwick-agents key set goose ...' are passed as environment variables

entries.name: cybara
entries.title: Cybara
entries.description: Self-hosted open-source AI agent platform: gateway, web dashboard and terminal UI
entries.mcp_hint: Cybara keeps MCP servers in its database: in the dashboard open Settings > MCP Servers and add the command /usr/bin/kwick-mcp

unsupported.riscv64: Cybara publishes x64 and arm64 builds only

entries.verify: sha256 pinned by KwickOS; equal to the vendor's .sha256 sidecar and checksums.txt
entries.upstream_install: curl -fsSL https://cybara.ai/install.sh | bash (same binary, checked against the .sha256 sidecar)

entries.name: ollama
entries.title: Ollama
entries.description: Run open models locally (Llama, Qwen, Gemma, DeepSeek and more) behind an API on port 11434

unsupported.riscv64: Ollama publishes amd64 and arm64 builds only

entries.verify: sha256 pinned by KwickOS; equal to the vendor's sha256sum.txt in the GitHub release
entries.upstream_install: curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh (no checksum check; creates a system user and service, may add the NVIDIA CUDA repository)
entries.first_run: run 'ollama serve' in one terminal and 'ollama run qwen3' in another
entries.notes: No system service and no extra user are created; models live in ~/.ollama. The sandbox gives it the GPU devices.

entries.name: llama-cpp
entries.title: llama.cpp
entries.description: LLM inference in C/C++: llama-cli and an OpenAI-compatible llama-server (CPU build)

unsupported.riscv64: no riscv64 build is published; build it from source

entries.verify: sha256 pinned by KwickOS; equal to the GitHub release asset digest
entries.upstream_install: download a release archive from GitHub
